title: Sky School · Voyager 1 is one light-day away

post.title: Voyager 1 is now a whole light-day from Earth 🛰️
post.description:
On 18 November 2026 at 10:16 UTC (11:16 CET), Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object one light-day from Earth: about 26 billion km, the distance light travels in 24 hours. A command from Earth now takes a full day to reach it, and the reply another day to come back. It took 49 years, two months and 11 days to get there.

Source:
NASA Science, Voyager 1: What Is a Light-Day: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/voyager/voyager-1/voyager-1-what-is-a-light-day/

Images: NASA / JPL / JPL-Caltech / KSC (Voyager 1 launch), NASA / JPL / MDSCC / INTA, Francisco "Paco" Moreno (Deep Space Network antennas near Madrid), NASA / JPL-Caltech (Pale Blue Dot). Narration uses a synthetic voice.

narration: Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth.
On the 18th of November it became the first human-made object this far away.
A light-day is how far light travels in twenty-four hours: about twenty-six billion kilometres.
Light reaches the Moon in 1.3 seconds, and the Sun in eight minutes and twenty seconds.
Voyager 1 is a whole day away.
So every command sent from Earth now takes a full day to arrive.
The reply takes another day to come back.
Getting there took forty-nine years, two months and eleven days, at nearly sixty-one thousand kilometres an hour.

params.label: 2 months and 11 days, at nearly 61,000 km/h

narration: And it is still sending data home.
It just arrives a day late.
